format: The shared Markdown corpus. Core (Markdown.test.ts), Rust (tests/markdown.rs) and the native engine (packages/native/src/tests/markdown_test.zig) run this file. A row is [name, chunks, html, fails, text?].

name starts with the row's source: spec (CommonMark 0.31.2), gfm (GFM 0.29-gfm extension examples), parity (Core and Rust disagreements, records 540, 561, 567), fixture (whole documents), reflow and stream (chunked streams), align (table column alignment), math (extensions: ["math"]), review (the M1 reviews' differential against cmark-gfm 27d942c8: each row takes the spec's answer, cmark-gfm's where it follows the spec, else the side the cited rule supports).
chunks are the appends of a stream; the document is their concatenation. A runner streams a row in its chunks, or a one-chunk row in 32 pieces of equal code point count.

html is what the specs say the whole document renders to, as its source publishes it, with the GFM extensions on. A runner compares it with an implementation's HTML after a subset of what both specs' test runners normalize (normalize.py): it drops newlines next to block tags (p, h1-h6, pre, ul, ol, li, blockquote, hr, table, thead, tbody, tr, th, td) and after
, the slash of the void tags br, hr, img and input, and writes ' as '. Spaces, tabs, other characters, other entities and raw HTML stay as they are. Math rows use and code blocks of the language math (tracks/markdown-extensions-1464.md).

fails lists the checks that disagree with the row, so the side the spec says is right is the row: engine-html (the native engine, which the Rust widget runs on, through its test HTML emitter) engine-stream (the native engine streamed against a fresh doc of the same source after each chunk, and against the whole document at the end; packages/native/src/tests/markdown_test.zig), and core-text:N, rust-text:N and engine-text:N (frame N, counted from 1). A check fails a row whose result does not match its listing, either way.

text, when present, holds the frame shown after each chunk, 60 columns wide with markup concealed, each line trimmed at its end: the first paint after a streamed chunk, and after the last chunk the frame once streaming has ended. Streams hold back what could still change kind (D93 Q4 B).

Rows named `spec N` are example N of the CommonMark Spec 0.31.2 by John MacFarlane (https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/), released under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/; LICENSE-COMMONMARK-SPEC). Rows named `gfm N` are example N of the GitHub Flavored Markdown Spec 0.29-gfm (https://github.github.com/gfm/), a derivative of the CommonMark Spec by GitHub, Inc., also under CC BY-SA 4.0. Their markdown and HTML are copied unchanged (the specs show a tab as →), except that examples 608, 611 and 612 take the GFM extended-autolink answer of cmark-gfm. This file is an adaptation shared under the same license.
